name: Inkvolt Print
subtitle: Printer status, ink and toner
promotionalText: See every printer's status, ink and toner levels and alerts at a glance, in its window or from the menu bar. No account, no cloud, no tracking.
description: Inkvolt Print keeps an eye on your printers. It finds them on your network and shows what matters: ready or asleep, ink and toner levels, paper and cover problems, and how many pages they've printed, kept up to date while it runs.
• Finds the printers on your network by itself.
• Ink and toner levels with the pages left, and the cartridge to buy when one runs low.
• Paper jams, empty trays, open covers and other problems, in plain words.
• A menu bar item shows at a glance whether every printer is fine, and a notification tells you when one needs you.
• Made for HP printers and works with Canon, Epson, Brother and other AirPrint, Mopria or IPP Everywhere printers. Older network printers get status and toner over SNMP.
• Before it shows anything, it checks that the device at a printer's address is still your printer, so another device that took the address is never shown under its name.
• Printers set up in macOS show too, USB and shared ones included, with their status and your print jobs, which you can cancel.
• A printer that stopped printing gets step-by-step help: Inkvolt Print finds it at a new address, resumes a paused queue and cancels stuck jobs, and says what to do in System Settings for the rest.

• Scan from the printer's scanner or a USB scanner: blank pages left out, crooked pages straightened, pages turned, cropped and reordered before you save them as a PDF, a searchable PDF (text recognised on your Mac) or JPEG images. One-click scan presets save where you choose, and can print a copy or attach the files to an email.

• Scan a stack from the feeder and split it into separate files at separator sheets or blank pages. Lay several photos on the glass and each is saved on its own, cut out straight; adjust any of them by hand.
• Print a PDF, make a copy, or copy both sides of an ID card onto one page.
• Print photos at their real size (full page, standard photo sizes, contact sheets) on the printer's own paper sizes, borderless where it offers it, with the paper type and quality you pick.
• Set up a network printer in macOS with one click, so every app can print to it.
• Change an HP printer's settings (sleep, two-sided printing, paper) and its automatic firmware updates, and run its maintenance pages.
• Add a printer that doesn't announce itself: Inkvolt Print searches your network for it, or takes its address.
• A demo with made-up printers, to try it without one.
Private by design: no account, no cloud service, no ads, no analytics, no tracking. Inkvolt Print talks only to the printers on your network.
Free and open source (MIT License). Source code: https://github.com/gabandres/inkvolt

Inkvolt Print is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by HP Inc., Canon, Seiko Epson or Brother. HP is a trademark of HP Inc. Canon, Epson and Brother are trademarks of their owners. They are used only to describe the printers Inkvolt Print works with.
reviewNotes: Inkvolt Print reads the status, alerts and ink or toner levels of printers on the user's local network. There is no account or sign-in.

Without a printer: when none is found (after about 30 seconds of looking), the window says "No printers found" and offers "Try the Demo", which opens a second window with made-up printers (five on the network, three set up in macOS) that answer from data built into the app (nothing goes to the network).

In the demo window: the Scan tab (on the demo inkjet or the USB laser) scans made-up pages and saves them where you choose; the demo office laser's Fix It… shows the offline fixer; the office MFP's print queue card shows made-up jobs; Print a PDF and Print Photos open the macOS print panel (Cancel stops them); the demo printer's Settings tab takes changes but the made-up printer keeps none.

Local Network: macOS asks for Local Network access at first launch. The app uses it to find printers with Bonjour (the service types listed in NSBonjourServices) and to read them over HTTP and HTTPS (IPP, and HP's own LEDM and CDM interfaces) and over SNMP. If access is denied, the app says so and links to System Settings.

Entitlements: com.apple.security.network.client for those connections; com.apple.security.network.server only to receive the UDP replies to the SNMP requests the app sends to printers on port 161 (how it reads a printer's status and supply levels, and how the network search finds printers: one request to the subnet's broadcast address). The app runs no server and accepts no incoming connections; every exchange starts with a request from the app. In the App Sandbox, receiving those UDP replies needs this entitlement: we tested a sandboxed build without it, and the request went out but receiving the printer's reply failed with EPERM; com.apple.security.print to read the printers set up in macOS (their CUPS queues: USB printers and printers shared from other computers are listed with their status) and to cancel the user's own print jobs, through libcups; com.apple.security.files.user-selected.read-write to save scans where the user chooses in the save panel; com.apple.security.files.bookmarks.app-scope to remember the folder the user chose for a scan preset; com.apple.security.device.usb to scan with USB scanners through ImageCaptureCore; com.apple.security.application-groups (AE6TTXW92K.com.bermudezsystems.inkvolt, our team's group) to keep an optional Inkvolt Pro licence key in one file that our other app, Inkvolt PDF, reads too, so a key entered in either app counts in both, and a list of the printers it knows (their names and network addresses, no keys or settings) that Inkvolt PDF reads to show a printer's status in its print panel. No key is needed: everything in the app works without one, and the app sells nothing.
The app collects no data. Everything it remembers stays in its container on the Mac.
whatsNew: • Scan clean up (Scan settings › Clean up, and in each preset): crop to the paper, whiten the background, descreen printed pictures, restore faded colors. Clean Up… on a page shows it large to try each one, Show as scanned to compare, and All Pages; Undo puts a clean up back.

• Searchable PDFs keep text in every language your Mac reads, Russian, Arabic, Chinese, Japanese and Korean included, so Preview and other PDF apps find it; choose the Text language for a scan or a preset.

• USB printers that print without a driver (IPP over USB) show their own ink or toner levels and status, read from the printer itself; the status card says where its status came from, and a printer that reports no levels says so.

• Job notifications (Settings › Alerts, off until you turn them on): when your own print job fails or stops moving, a notification names the document and the printer, with Open the Queue and Pause Alerts. Other people's jobs never raise one.

• Ink and toner history: Inkvolt Print keeps a reading a day on your Mac and shows a chart of the levels over the last year, about how many days each cartridge has left, and how many pages you've printed since it went in. Low-ink alerts say how many days are left too. Export history… saves it all as one spreadsheet file (an Inkvolt Pro feature, free for now).

• Firmware watch: when a printer's firmware changes, its status card says so. HP printers: Keep My Cartridges Working, in the Settings tab, turns automatic firmware updates off, so an update that blocks non-HP cartridges can't install by itself.
• Scanners that send only PDF work, and a scan saved untouched is kept exactly as the scanner sent it.
• Help › Inkvolt Pro…: enter an Inkvolt Pro key; Inkvolt PDF on this Mac finds it too.
• Inkvolt PDF on this Mac shows the status and toner of your printers here when you print, and warns before printing to one that's off or jammed.

• Help › Report a Problem…: the details a bug report needs, with addresses, serial numbers and your names masked, to copy into a GitHub issue. Record This Printer saves what the printer shown answers, read only and with what identifies it taken out, as a .zip to attach. Nothing is sent.

• Fleet, at the top of the sidebar (View › Fleet): every printer on one page, the ones in trouble first, with each one's ink or toner, page count, firmware and when it was last read; a printer that isn't answering shows what it last said. Export… saves the list as a spreadsheet or JSON, and Fix All resumes paused printers and lets them accept jobs again, asking before each one (Inkvolt Pro features, free for now). From Terminal, “Inkvolt Print status --all --json” lists every printer for a script.

• Batch Print (File › Batch Print…): add PDFs and pictures, or a whole folder, put them in order and see how many sheets each one takes before anything prints. Print sends them to the printer one by one, asks first when a batch comes to more than 100 sheets, and Stop stops between files; a file that changed or needs a password is never printed by surprise. Save a list to print again, print a folder as files land in it, save the results as a spreadsheet, and print a list from Terminal with “Inkvolt Print print --list” (Inkvolt Pro features, free for now).

• Open in Inkvolt PDF, when it's installed on this Mac: a scan preset can open its PDFs there, Settings › General's Open scans in Inkvolt PDF opens each saved scan, and the save bar offers it after a PDF is saved.
